content.value_statement: Narrow, dark hallways can limit storage and make renovation decisions difficult. This skill uses Chinese reference articles to explain practical options and common mistakes.
actual_capabilities: Consult local reference articles before answering hallway renovation questions.
Compare shallow cabinets, recessed storage, bookshelves, niches, and pegboards.
Explain daylight borrowing, mirrors, sensor lights, and supplemental lighting options.
Discuss ceiling treatments and visual approaches for exposed hallway beams.
Suggest hallway utility storage and bathroom vanity relocation concepts.
Organize answers into conclusions, detailed analysis, practical actions, and common mistakes.
limitations: Provides design guidance, not structural assessments, construction drawings, or code certification.
References include duplicated passages, missing image context, and text-extraction errors.
Does not verify current prices, regulations, or the freshness of advice labeled 2026.
Demolition, recessed storage, and utility relocation require qualified professionals to verify structure, services, waterproofing, and local requirements.

use_cases.title: Choose Storage for a Narrow Hallway
use_cases.description: Compare shallow cabinets, shelves, and pegboards using measured clearances and household storage needs.

use_cases.title: Prepare Lighting Alternatives
use_cases.description: Develop daylight, mirror, and fixture options for a client discussion about a dark corridor.

use_cases.title: Review a Renovation Proposal
use_cases.description: Identify questions about cabinet access, ceiling height, circulation, and utility placement before construction discussions.

prompt_templates.title: Start With One Hallway Problem
prompt_templates.prompt: My hallway is [width] wide and [length] long. Suggest simple storage options without changing walls.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Lighting Options
prompt_templates.prompt: My hallway has [daylight conditions], [ceiling height], and [budget]. Compare mirrors, sensor lights, and ceiling lights using the references.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Cabinet Proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this hallway cabinet proposal: [details]. Check circulation, door swings, storage priorities, and missing measurements. List questions for my contractor.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Hallway Redesign
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [dimensions], [budget], and [constraints], compare storage, lighting, and utility layouts. Identify tradeoffs, dependencies, and professional checks before any demolition or relocation.

output_examples.input: My hallway is narrow. Can I add storage without removing walls?
output: Direct answer: Start with shallow shelves or a pegboard instead of a deep cabinet.
Detailed analysis: Measure the remaining passage and check nearby door swings before choosing cabinet depth.
Practical actions: List the objects you need to store and compare their dimensions with the available space.
Common mistakes: Do not copy another home's cabinet dimensions without checking your own circulation needs.

output_examples.input: My hallway is dark, and the ceiling is low. What should I consider?
output: Direct answer: Compare surface-mounted lighting and reflective finishes before choosing a full suspended ceiling.
Detailed analysis: A lowered ceiling can reduce an already limited sense of height.
Practical actions: Record beam heights, nearby daylight sources, and existing electrical points for a lighting discussion.
Common mistakes: Do not cut beams or open walls without qualified assessment and required approvals.

best_practices: Provide hallway dimensions, ceiling height, door positions, budget, and storage priorities before requesting recommendations.
Ask for the relevant reference topics and distinguish general examples from recommendations specific to your home.
Have qualified professionals verify structure, utilities, accessibility, and local requirements before approving construction changes.
anti_patterns: Treating confident renovation advice or the expert persona as proof of professional qualifications.
Copying cabinet dimensions or demolishing walls without checking clearances, structure, and concealed services.
Assuming the 2026 label guarantees current regulations, prices, or verified construction details.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers hallway storage, lighting, ceilings, beams, decorative finishes, and layout concepts using local Chinese reference articles.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What language are the source materials?
faq.answer: The instructions and reference articles are written in Chinese.

faq.question: Does it generate construction drawings or renderings?
faq.answer: No drawing or rendering workflow is included. The skill provides conversational advice and can discuss supplied plans or photos when supported.

faq.question: Can it approve wall demolition or plumbing changes?
faq.answer: No. Qualified professionals must assess structure, concealed services, waterproofing, and local requirements before those changes proceed.

faq.question: Does the skill retrieve live prices or updated regulations?
faq.answer: No live retrieval workflow is included. Check current local prices and requirements independently.
